limits.text: Venice takes at most 5 reference images and videos together in one request. Dez checks the image count and the video count apart (at most 5 each), not their sum.
limits.source: Venice API reference of POST /video/queue (image_references, video_references): https://docs.venice.ai/api-reference/endpoint/video/queue

limits.text: The Venice docs give no size or length limit of the voice of a reference (audio_url), and Dez checks none. A long or large voice clip can get a refusal from Venice.
limits.source: Venice API reference of POST /video/queue (image_references[].audio_url, video_references[].audio_url): https://docs.venice.ai/api-reference/endpoint/video/queue

limits.text: Venice takes reference videos and a video length (duration) of at most 30 seconds together. Dez does not check that sum: Venice refuses such a job when Dez asks for its result, and gives the charge back.

Dez sends each image as the front image of one element (@Element1, @Element2, …). It sends no video of an element (elements[].video_url), no other images of an element, and no scene images (scene_image_urls). This is a limit of Dez, not of the model.
limits.source: Dez. The fields are in the Venice API reference of POST /video/queue: https://docs.venice.ai/api-reference/endpoint/video/queue

limits.text: Venice takes a request body of at most 35 MB. Dez sends each image and clip of the request in that body as a data URL (about a third larger than its file) and does not check the body size, so the files of one request must stay under about 25 MB together.
Venice takes an input image of an edit only under 25 MB. Dez does not check the file size, so a larger image gets a refusal.
Venice takes a reference image of at most 30 MB. Dez does not check the file size.
This model takes no last frame: Venice refuses a request with two images (end_image_url), at no cost. Send one image, the first frame.
limits.source: Venice's answer to a request with a first and a last frame
